basis: Complex congenital cardiac defects and asplenia define the syndrome; abnormal organ position and lung lobation alone do not establish damage.
Benign brown-fat tumor arising within the central nervous system.
Typically an epididymal or broad-ligament epithelial tumor, both reproductive sites outside the axes; this record specifies no alternative site.
Autoimmune inflammation of the optic nerve; the optic nerve belongs to the ocular axis.
Demyelinating peripheral neuropathy; fixed foot deformities include pes cavus in 4/4 and hammertoes in 3/4 patients.
Primary skeletal dysplasia; motor delay can reflect skeletal limitations. Cord damage and functionally significant airway calcification lack established >=30% frequency.
Neoplasm of urinary tract urothelium; the renal axis includes bladder, ureters and urethra.
Myofibroblastic neoplasm arising in the bladder; its inflammatory infiltrate does not establish an immune-mediated disease.
Disease located in a tendon sheath; no additional organ applies across this umbrella.
Malignancy involving the larynx, which belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Cutaneous capillary malformation involving dermal vessels; associated hyperkeratosis and hair/nail abnormalities remain within the skin axis.
Isolated developmental eye disorder with microphthalmia and displaced pupils.
CNS germ-cell tumor of the pineal region; regional location does not establish an endocrine gland disorder.
Autoinflammatory syndrome defined by destructive skin inflammation and axial inflammatory arthritis.
Persistent tongue depapillation and inflammation, commonly attributable to chronic Candida infection; mouth belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Ataxia and generalized skin pigmentation define this variant; the parent disorder includes combined immunodeficiency. Common pulmonary damage is not established here.
Microcephaly and intellectual disability define the disorder; optic neuropathy affects 2/6 (~33%). Skeletal dysmorphism alone does not establish locomotor damage.
Benign cutaneous vascular tumor characterized by hobnail endothelial cells.
Congenital skin and hair-associated hamartoma; subsequent melanoma is a separate disease risk.
Congenital splitting of the spinal cord within a single dural sac.
Microphthalmia 80-99%; adrenal/thyroid/pituitary defects 30-79%. GI atresia/clefts and cardiac defects (30-79%) omitted at cap; brain and polydactyly define syndrome.
Inherited febrile seizure disorder; seizures documented in 20/20 patients.
Infantile focal epilepsy defined by seizures and characteristic sleep EEG findings.
Inherited hyaline deposition disorder; laryngeal infiltration/hoarseness ~100%, oral lesions 80-99%. Neurologic features reported at 30-79% omitted at cap.
Neonatal conjunctival inflammation, usually infectious and classified under gonococcal conjunctivitis; definition also encompasses chemical cases.
